definition: Communal nursing refers to a caregiving pattern observed in mice in which nursing of young occurs in a shared social setting. In the source, it is described as part of normal mother-young behavior seen in both wild and laboratory environments.

reasons: Field mismatch: the packet describes an ethological observation in mice (communal nursing) rather than a psychological/clinical diagnosis.

Unsupported characterization: the definition claims this is “normal mother-young behavior”; the packet only states that mice “display … communal nursing in wild and laboratory environments” and does not explicitly frame it as “normal” or “mother-young behavior.”
Only partially supported wording: “shared social setting” is implied by “communal nursing,” but the packet does not explicitly describe a “shared social setting” in those terms.
The packet supports that mice display communal nursing in wild and laboratory environments, but it does not support the added claim that this is described as a normal mother-young behavior.
The definition is framed as a diagnostic/clinical concept, but the source term is a rodent behavioral observation, so the field sense is not defensible here.
